results.identification: A condensed, unofficial summary of the UK Labour Party’s 2019 General Election manifesto (“It’s Time For Real Change”), derived from that manifesto.
results.evidence: The heading says “Labour Party Manifesto 2019 – Summary.” Content matches distinctive 2019 UK Labour policies: “It’s time for real change” framing; raise income tax above £80k; £400bn National Transformation Fund incl. £250bn Green fund; free full‑fibre broadband by 2030 via public ownership; bring rail into public ownership; 32‑hour week; abolish tuition fees; 1m climate jobs; ban fracking; final‑say referendum within six months; abolish the House of Lords for an elected Senate; end the hostile environment; scrap Universal Credit; maintain NATO/2% and renew Trident.

results.identification: A bullet‑point summary of the UK Liberal Democrats’ 2019 General Election manifesto (“Stop Brexit. Build a Brighter Future”), derived from the party’s official manifesto.
results.evidence: The heading says “Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2019 – summary”; distinctive Lib Dem 2019 pledges appear throughout, e.g. “Stop Brexit… use a £50bn ‘Remain Bonus’”, “1p on Income Tax… ringfenced for NHS and social care”, “Proportional representation (STV)”, “Skills Wallet: £10,000 per adult”, “replace Business Rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy”, “all new cars/vans electric by 2030”, and “recognise Palestine”.

results.identification: An unofficial, third‑party 500‑word summary of the Scottish National Party’s 2019 UK General Election manifesto, likely taken from a manifesto‑summaries compilation or blog rather than the SNP’s official publication.
results.evidence: The heading explicitly says “Scottish National Party Manifesto 2019 – Summary (≤500 words)”. The content matches distinctive SNP 2019 GE positions: a new independence referendum via Section 30, support for a UK‑wide second EU referendum, scrapping Trident, devolving immigration and employment law, opposing the £30k salary threshold, a Scottish Visa, backing WASPI women, protecting the NHS from trade deals, and climate targets aligned with Scotland’s (75% by 2030; net‑zero carbon by 2040; all GHGs by 2045). The structured, bullet‑point, synopsis style indicates it is a condensed, third‑party summary rather than the full official manifesto.

results.identification: An unofficial condensed summary of the Green Party of England & Wales’ 2019 UK General Election manifesto (“If not now, when?”) and its costings—compiled from the party’s policies rather than an official text excerpt.
results.evidence: The header explicitly says “Green Party Manifesto 2019 – Summary.” Content matches the Green Party of England & Wales’ 2019 UK General Election manifesto: net‑zero by 2030 via a Green New Deal; UBI at £89/week for adults and £178/week for pensioners; remain in the EU via a People’s Vote; cancel Trident and HS2; no new road capacity or runways; ban fracking and no new nuclear; proportional representation; votes at 16; scrap tuition fees and write off £9k‑era debt; Land Value Tax; carbon tax raising ~£76.7bn.

results.identification: A neutral, bullet‑point synopsis of the UK Conservative Party’s 2019 General Election manifesto, “Get Brexit Done: Unleash Britain’s Potential,” condensed from the official manifesto published in November 2019.
results.evidence: Distinctive 2019 UK Conservative manifesto pledges appear throughout: “Get Brexit Done” timetable (no extension beyond Dec 2020), FTAs with US/AUS/NZ/Japan and up to 10 freeports; no rises in main income tax/NI/VAT rates and raising the NI threshold to £9,500; 50,000 more nurses; 6,000 more GPs and 50m more GP appointments; 40 new hospitals; 20,000 extra police; Australian-style points-based immigration; end ‘no‑fault’ evictions; target 300,000 homes a year; gigabit broadband nationwide by 2025 with £5bn for hard‑to‑reach areas; SME R&D tax credit to 13% and a new high‑risk research agency; leave the Common Fisheries Policy; Environment Bill with a new watchdog, 40GW offshore wind by 2030, fracking moratorium, £500m Blue Planet Fund; repeal the Fixed-term Parliaments Act, voter ID; exceed NATO 2% with 0.5% real growth; maintain 0.7% aid and introduce Magnitsky sanctions; tougher animal welfare laws and ban on trophy hunting imports.

results.identification: A neutral, bullet‑point ‘ideology‑free’ summary of the UK Labour Party’s 2019 General Election manifesto (“It’s Time for Real Change”), as compiled by Ben Goldacre in his public Google Doc summary of the manifesto (November 2019).
results.evidence: Mentions a £400bn National Transformation Fund with a £250bn Green Transformation Fund; public ownership of rail, buses, energy and water; free full‑fibre broadband by 2030 via a public provider; £10 Real Living Wage and 32‑hour week; abolish tuition fees; bring academies/free schools under local oversight; end Right to Buy; abolish the House of Lords and replace with an elected Senate; recognise Palestine; retain NATO/2% defence and renew the nuclear deterrent; Brexit plan of a new customs‑union‑based deal put to a confirmatory referendum alongside remain within six months. These are hallmark planks of the UK Labour Party’s 2019 general election manifesto.

results.identification: A condensed, paraphrased summary of the UK Liberal Democrats’ 2019 General Election manifesto (“Stop Brexit. Build a Brighter Future.”), i.e., the Liberal Democrats’ official 2019 policy platform.
results.evidence: “Revoke Article 50 to remain in the EU if winning a majority; otherwise back a referendum with an option to remain.”; “Skills Wallets of £10,000 per adult for lifelong learning”; “+1p on Income Tax … for NHS and social care”; “Replace Business Rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy”; “Net‑zero by 2045” and plant “60m trees/year”; “Young People’s Premium”; “Replace Police and Crime Commissioners with local boards”; “decriminalise possession for personal use” and a “regulated cannabis market”; electoral reform to “Single Transferable Vote … votes at 16”; “maintain 0.7% aid … minimum nuclear deterrent (reduced fleet, altered posture).”

results.identification: A neutral bullet‑point summary of the Scottish National Party (SNP) manifesto for the 2019 UK general election, drawn from the SNP’s 2019 manifesto.
results.evidence: References to a second Scottish independence referendum; devolving immigration to create a Scottish Visa; Scottish‑specific climate targets (net zero by 2045, 75% by 2030); growing the Scottish National Investment Bank; devolved broadcasting powers; cancellation of the UK’s nuclear weapons (Trident) while retaining bases/regiments; free higher education in Scotland; agriculture convergence uplift and fisheries lines specific to Scotland.

results.identification: A condensed bullet-point summary of the Green Party of England and Wales’ 2019 UK General Election manifesto (“If Not Now, When?”), drawn from the party’s official manifesto/costings materials.
results.evidence: Mentions specific Green Party 2019 planks, e.g.: “A 10-year Green New Deal to reach net-zero emissions by 2030… over £100bn a year… £94.4bn a year of public capital borrowing”; “no new nuclear; ban fracking”; “Frequent Flyer Levy”; “cancel HS2”; “plant 700m trees”; “Nature GCSE”; “Universal Basic Income: adults £89/week; pensioners £178/week”; “replace Council Tax and Business Rates with a Land Value Tax”; “cancel Trident replacement.” These are distinctive to the Green Party of England & Wales’ 2019 manifesto.
